summary: Reynolds County, MO: a Forest Service lookout platform in a tall tree, described in a 1938 survey; the record's 'tower' kind does not fit.

facts.design: Forest Service lookout platform in a tall tree (1938 survey description)

evidence.supports: site described as a tree crow's nest lookout
county and forest named on the page
evidence.quote: Missouri Lookouts - Reynolds County - Mark Twain National Forest - 32N-1E-9

evidence.supports: survey marker on the east end of a high, wooded ridge
evidence.quote: STATION CENTERVILLE IS ON THE EAST END OF A HIGH, WOODED RIDGE

evidence.supports: prominent hill about 3 miles north of Centerville
evidence.quote: AND A PROMINENT HILL LYING ABOUT 3 MILES NORTH OF CENTERVILLE
DESCRIBED BY COAST AND GEODETIC SURVEY 1938 (CDM)

evidence.supports: marker 70 feet southwest of a Forest Service platform in a tall tree
evidence.quote: 70 FEET SOUTHWEST OF A UNITED STATES FOREST SERVICE LOOKOUT PLATFORM IN A TALL TREE

evidence.supports: marker half a mile northeast of a CCC camp on the Centerville-Bixby road
evidence.quote: 1/2 MILE NORTHEAST OF A CIVILIAN CONSERVATION CORPS CAMP ON THE CENTERVILLE-BIXBY ROAD

evidence.supports: access directions: the station is at the top of the hill, which supports 'at the top of a prominent hill'
evidence.quote: TO THE TOP OF HILL AND THE STATION ON THE LEFT

evidence.supports: today: the page has no description of the site now; this quote is its only lookout description

corrections.why: The page calls it a tree crow's nest lookout, and the 1938 survey description places a Forest Service platform in a tall tree, not a tower on legs. The kind is for a human to confirm, since tree sites are the no-structure group.

notes_for_editor: Single source: the Central US Lookouts page, which quotes the National Geodetic Survey station description (1938). The NGS datasheet itself was not fetched. The page gives no build date, staffing, fire history, or fate, so the story is short. Searches found no Missouri register listing and no other Centerville lookout history. The kind correction (tower to tree) is for a human to decide, since tree sites are in the no-structure group.
